historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: weighted category growth (~1.7% K-C categories, ~3% consumer health) -- equity CAGR unusable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (32.6% / 13.4%) diverges far more than 30% from revenue and EPS CAGRs and is meaningless: book equity was ~0.7-1.6bn after decades of buybacks, and jumps again with the IFP gain and the Kenvue share issue. Not used.
historical_growth.notes: All history is K-C STANDALONE and says little about the combined company. Revenue 3-year is continuing operations (North America + International Personal Care: 16,524 in FY2022 to 16,447 in FY2025); the 5-year figure is on a total-company basis (19,140 in FY2020 to ~19,750 including IFP in FY2025) because FY2020-22 rows in the CSV pre-date the discontinued-operations restatement. EPS is diluted GAAP (FY2022 5.72, FY2020 6.87, FY2025 6.07). FCF CAGRs use owner FCF = reported FCF less SBC (FY2020 2,365, FY2022 1,707, FY2025 1,499); FY2025 is depressed by Transformation Initiative capex and cash charges. Reported-FCF CAGRs are within a point of these: SBC is not the story here.

scenario_narratives.base: The combination works, but only partly. Legacy K-C categories (diapers, adult and feminine care, tissue in North America) grow about 1-2% against falling birth rates and private-label pressure; Kenvue's self-care, skin health and oral/wound-care brands grow about 3%, giving 2-3% for the group once the China social-media disruption and the Arbex supply-agreement sales wash through 2027. About 60% of the $2.1bn net synergy target reaches the margin by year 4, lifting pre-SBC EBITDA from a pro forma 23.5% in FY2026 to 27%, where it stays. The $2.5bn of cash integration cost and a probability-weighted Tylenol reserve are deducted in the bridge. Starting leverage is about 2.5x net debt to EBITDA and the $5.04 dividend on 616m shares takes roughly $3.1bn a year, so deleveraging is slow and buybacks are absent for several years. The base year is an analyst pro forma: the trailing filings are K-C standalone and no combined guidance has been issued.
scenario_narratives.bull: Management delivers the plan. The full $1.9bn of cost synergies lands inside three years and revenue synergies follow as Kenvue brands ride K-C's emerging-market distribution and K-C brands enter the pharmacy channel; Powering Care productivity (~$460-500m a year gross) keeps funding brand investment. Growth runs 3-4% as the mix tilts toward consumer health, EBITDA margin reaches 29.5%, the Tylenol suits are dismissed again or settle inside the reserve, and the Arbex option is exercised at or above carrying value.
scenario_narratives.bear: The deal proves a diversification too far. ERP and supply-chain integration across two different operating models disrupts service; Kenvue's skin-health business, which was already losing share before the deal, keeps shrinking; private label and promotion take price in diapers and tissue; and Tylenol volumes weaken under label changes and litigation headlines. Sales grow 0-1%, synergies only offset dis-synergies and price investment so margin peaks at 24.5%, and the acetaminophen litigation resolves well above the reserve -- carried here as ~1.2pp of margin drag in years 2-5. Leverage stays above 2.5x, the dividend absorbs nearly all free cash flow, and the market pays 15x terminal free cash flow at most.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Kimberly-Clark is valued as the combined post-Kenvue company on an owner-FCF basis: unlevered free cash flow after stock compensation, built from components over ten years on a pro forma FY2026 base, less pro forma net debt, with the equity-method stakes, minorities, pensions, integration cash costs and a litigation reserve in the equity bridge. The trailing financials on file are K-C standalone continuing operations; Kenvue's contribution comes from its own SEC filings through Q3-2026 and the pro forma is the analyst's, not the company's. Synergies are credited at about 60% of target in the base case. The share count, net debt and base-year margin are all estimates that the FY2026 10-K will replace, and the valuation should be rebuilt when it is filed.
key_risks_to_valuation: Pro forma base: FY2026 combined sales, margin, net debt (~18.65bn) and diluted shares (~615.6m) are analyst-built; a 1pp error in the base EBITDA margin moves value by roughly 7 per share
Synergy delivery: each $500m of run-rate synergy retained is worth roughly 9-10 per share
Tylenol/acetaminophen-autism litigation: 500+ revived suits and the Texas AG action; the $1.5bn after-tax reserve is a judgment, and each further $1bn after tax is ~1.60 per share
Dividend cover and leverage: ~$3.1bn of dividends against ~$3.4bn of post-interest free cash flow before ~$1bn a year of integration cash in 2027-28
Terminal value: the 18x cap binds in base and bull, so value is set by year-10 free cash flow and the multiple rather than by Gordon growth
K-C de Mexico stake capitalised from equity income rather than marked to its listed price
Structural volume pressure in Baby & Child Care (birth rates in the US, China, South Korea) and private-label share gains

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 92.42-116.82
data_sources.financials: KMB_Metrics.csv and KMB.duckdb (K-C standalone, continuing operations); KMB 10-Q Q3-2026 (balance sheet, cash flow, adjusted operating profit reconciliation, Kenvue acquisition, financing and integration-program notes); KMB 10-K FY2025; Kenvue Inc. SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 1944048) through its Q3-2026 10-Q for sales, operating income, D&A, SBC, capex, operating cash flow, debt, cash and shares

inputs.share_count_basis: PRO FORMA post-Kenvue close, analyst-built: 333.7m K-C diluted weighted shares (Q3-2026 10-Q EPS note) + 281.1m shares delivered to Kenvue holders on 2026-11-02 (10-Q subsequent-events note; ties to 1,921.8m Kenvue shares x 0.14625) + ~0.8m for converted Kenvue equity awards (Kenvue diluted less basic, x exchange ratio). No post-close diluted count is in XBRL yet; replace with the FY2026 10-K figure. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: Cash-flow-statement add-backs, trailing twelve months to Q3-2026: K-C 131 (FY2025 140 - 9M-2025 115 + 9M-2026 106, KMB 10-K/10-Q) + Kenvue 120 (136 - 106 + 90, Kenvue SEC XBRL companyfacts). Neither filer publishes a combined SBC-plus-withholding-tax figure and the withholding tax is not broken out of 'Other' financing, so the charge is the add-back only; at 0.8% of sales the omission is small.
inputs.fy0: FY2026 pro forma (K-C continuing ops + Kenvue, full year)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-13T21:00:01Z regular close (first eight sessions after the Kenvue close, so it prices the combined company)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free ~4.3% (10-year UST), equity risk premium ~4.75%, staples/consumer-health beta ~0.7 -> cost of equity ~7.6%; after-tax cost of debt ~4.3% (new notes priced 5.10-5.80%); ~78/22 equity/debt at market -> ~6.9%, rounded UP to 7.5% for the elevated post-deal leverage. One WACC for all three scenarios: integration, leverage and litigation risk is carried by the scenario paths, the weights and the bridge reserve, not by a second premium in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases stay in the flows (US GAAP operating lease cost sits inside EBITDA); lease liabilities (~429 K-C + ~150 Kenvue) are NOT in net debt. One treatment only.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated; minority interests (K-C subsidiaries, ~30/yr of income, 142 book + 22 redeemable preferred) are deducted once in the equity bridge at ~15x earnings.
inputs.pro_forma_basis: The Metrics CSV is K-C standalone continuing operations and contains no Kenvue. FY0 is an analyst-built pro forma for calendar 2026: K-C 9M-2026 actuals + a Q4 estimate (sales ~16,590; adjusted operating profit ~2,820 per mid-single-digit growth guidance; D&A ~720; SBC ~140) plus Kenvue 9M-2026 actuals from its own SEC XBRL filings + a Q4 estimate (sales ~15,650; operating income ex restructuring and deal costs ~3,215 after intangible amortisation; D&A ~575; SBC ~120). Combined: sales 32,240, EBITDA before SBC ~7,590 (23.5%), SBC ~260, D&A ~1,295, capex ~1,720. No company-issued combined guidance or Article 11 pro forma was available in the filings on hand; the FY2026 10-K will carry the purchase-price allocation and should replace this build.
inputs.net_debt_basis: PRO FORMA estimate, not a reported balance: K-C debt 6,491 less cash 1,874 at 2026-09-30, plus Kenvue debt 8,206 less cash 1,039 at 2026-09-27, plus the 6,700 cash consideration and ~170 of remaining deal fees = ~18,650. Funding mix (4,900 of new notes issued 2026-10-29, commercial paper, cash on hand) moves gross debt and cash but not the net figure; total_debt 20,150 / cash 1,500 is an assumed split. 6.4bn of Kenvue notes were exchanged into K-C notes on 2026-11-04, 0.6bn remain at Kenvue.
inputs.reported_fcf_basis: Trailing twelve months to Q3-2026, levered, both companies summed: K-C operating cash flow 3,380 less capex 1,436 = 1,944 (includes a one-off 444 receipt for the 30-year IP licence to the Arbex JV and IFP cash flows to 2026-06-30); Kenvue 2,731 less 393 = 2,338. Interest income is not stripped because the company is in net debt.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (margins are still ramping through the synergy period). Routed as a US consumer-staples operating company; no memory entry, first valuation. The company being valued is the COMBINED post-Kenvue entity (acquisition closed 2026-11-02; IFP contributed to the Arbex JV 2026-07-01), built on a pro forma FY2026 base because the trailing filings are K-C standalone -- see pro_forma_basis, net_debt_basis and share_count_basis; all three are analyst estimates pending the FY2026 10-K. No buybacks in 2026 (9M repurchases nil); the flat share count is a modelling convention that the SBC charge pays for, and deleveraging will take priority over repurchases. D&A path excludes the step-up intangible amortisation the purchase accounting will create: it is non-cash and, in a stock deal with carry-over tax basis, not deductible, so including it would understate cash tax. Equity income (K-C de Mexico, Arbex) is outside the flows and its assets are in the bridge. SBC is under 1% of sales, so house and street values sit close together.

bear.rationale: Margin path carries ~1.2pp/yr of drag in years 2-5 (~$1.6bn cumulative) as additional Tylenol litigation cost beyond the bridge reserve, on top of synergies that only offset dis-synergies and price investment.

base.rationale: Margin: 23.5% pro forma FY2026 rising 3.5pp, i.e. ~$1.3bn of the $2.1bn net synergy target retained by year 4 (about 60%; the rest reinvested, competed away in promotion, or not delivered). Capex: K-C ~$1.1bn + Kenvue ~$0.5bn in 2027 as the Transformation Initiative spend rolls off, settling near 5.5% of K-C sales and 3% of Kenvue sales. Cash tax: blend of K-C's ~22% adjusted rate and Kenvue's ~27.5%. Working capital: a small consumer of cash on growth (receivables + inventory roughly match payables at K-C; Kenvue runs positive working capital).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: a $48.7bn acquisition closed thirteen days ago, the base year is an analyst pro forma rather than reported, leverage is elevated and an open-ended litigation exposure was inherited. Base 50%: partial synergy delivery is the usual outcome for large consumer mergers. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs full cost synergies, revenue synergies and a benign litigation outcome together.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
